newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline sellers bear down.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline sellers bear down.

text.p: Gasoline prices edged down with more sellers emerging to bear down on prices, traders said on Monday.
Two sellers emerged to offer 95-octane and 97-octane unleaded 50,000 barrel cargoes for February lifting.
"The market is still tight but they can still squeeze out 50,000 barrels for end month," a trader said.
A Dutch trader offered 97-octane at $28.00 per barrel fob Singapore for February 22-25 lifting, lower than a major's bid at $28.15 for Feb 18-22 barrels. On Friday, bids/offers were $28.50/$27.90.
A late February cargo of 95-octane was offered at $26.90, while a buyer for 92-octane was heard just 10 cents lower.
"It is ridiculous," said one trader. "You might as well buy the 95, blend it and sell the 92-octane."

India's 87-octane leaded gasoline tender for February 21-25 delivery to the west coast, its third purchase for the month, was awarded at $2.50 per barrel c-and-f over Singapore 92-octane unleaded quotes to Swiss trader Glencore, Indian sources said.
South Korean Yukong Ltd extended its shutdown of 25,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) reformer production until February 9, an industry source said.
"It has been extended to after the Lunar New year holidays," the source said. "After that, the situation will be checked."
He said current reforming margins were still poor.
Bad margins prompted Yukong to stop production at its 10,000-bpd No.1 and 15,000-bpd No.2 reformers on January 24. The shutdown duration was initially for 10 to 15 days.
Naphtha fell with weaker crude and swaps levels. February swaps were around 60 cents lower at $24.30/$24.60 per barrel.
Although demand was lacklustre, most February barrels were already placed, traders said.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
